prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500 over a single year. In most years, the majority of professional large-cap fund managers underperform it, and over 15 years roughly 90% do (per S&P's SPIVA reports). Also, my information runs through May 2026, so prices, valuations and news since then aren't reflected. Treat this as a starting point for your own research, not a recommendation.

## 10 candidates

| # | Stock | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure growth, AI built into Office and enterprise software, strong pricing power | Heavy AI spending may take longer to pay off |
| 2 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search cash flow, Google Cloud momentum, Gemini, Waymo; often cheaper than its big-tech peers | Antitrust remedies; AI chatbots taking search share |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS, a fast-growing ad business, improving retail margins | Capex weighing on free cash flow; consumer slowdown |
| 4 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all leading-edge AI chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and others | Taiwan–China tensions; tariffs |
| 5 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers, AI networking, VMware software income | Depends on a few large customers; already richly valued |
| 6 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs; oral pipeline could widen the market | High valuation; drug-pricing pressure; competition |
| 7 | **Intuitive Surgical (ISRG)** | Dominant surgical-robot platform with recurring instrument revenue | Premium valuation; new robotic competitors |
| 8 | **Visa (V)** | Toll-road business model, high margins, steady growth in cross-border travel | Regulatory limits on fees; new payment methods |
| 9 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-run large bank; benefits from capital-markets activity and scale | Credit losses in a recession; interest-rate shifts |
| 10 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and grid equipment in demand from data-center power needs | Cyclical business; the stock has already rerated sharply |

Together these cover tech, semiconductors, healthcare, financials and industrials, so you aren't making a single bet.

## How to use this more safely

1. **Beating the index means being different from it.** Many of these are already large S&P 500 holdings, so this basket may track the index closely. Any real deviation, like more weight in fewer names, can just as easily lead to underperformance.
2. **Consider a core-and-satellite approach.** Keep most of your money (say 70–90%) in an S&P 500 index fund and put the rest in picks like these. You still get a chance to outperform without risking your whole portfolio.
3. **Check current valuations before buying.** Look at price-to-earnings versus growth and recent earnings reports, since a lot may have changed since May 2026.
4. **Size positions evenly and decide your exit rules in advance**, such as when you'd sell if the original reason for buying no longer holds.
5. **Think in more than one year.** Over 12 months, returns are driven mostly by market mood; over 3–5 years, business quality matters more.

If you tell me your risk tolerance, how much you're investing, and any sectors you prefer or want to avoid, I can tailor the list.
